title: streaming chunk stall breadcrumbs (personal scratchpad)
content:
Summary:
This is a personal scratchpad capturing a new variant of streaming failures where the client perceives a long stall between chunks even though the server appears to be emitting data. Different from prior partial-frame hangs: here we often see well-formed "chunks" (SSE data: lines ending with 

) but the client read stalls mid-response for 1–10s, then resumes with a burst of queued frames.

Symptoms observed: 
- Client (node-fetch / browser) shows data pauses ~2–8s during otherwise steady generation.
- Server-side logs show continuous token generation and write() calls with sub-100ms gaps.
- Kernel-level metrics show send queue (tcp_send_queue) growing during the stall then dropping when client finally receives.
- Not all requests reproduce; seems correlated with specific request patterns (long context + KV-cache warm path + small streaming window).

First seen: 2026-02-09 during canary of quantized-opt model on dedicated pool. Impact: intermittent UX jank on chat-like features; severity moderate.

Quick notes on differences from other bugs: 
- Unlike partial-frame hang, frames themselves are intact (no truncation markers).
- Unlike trailer-whitespace issues, the delimiter sequence is correct.
- Backpressure-like symptoms but server write()s don't block in userland; kernel-level backpressure appears to be throttling.

Repro attempt 1 — minimal curl SSE client (works intermittently):
Command:
  curl -v -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \n    -d '{"model":"quant-opt-1.2","prompt":"long prompt ...","stream":true}' \n    https://api.redwood.local/v1/generate/stream
Notes: curl sometimes shows continuous stream, sometimes stalls after ~20 tokens for ~3–6s then dumps several events.

Repro attempt 2 — Node streaming (consistent reproduction locally):
node repro-stream-client.js (attached below)\// repro-stream-client.js (snippet)
const fetch = require('node-fetch');
(async ()=>{
  const res = await fetch(url, { method: 'POST', headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${TOKEN}`, 'Accept': 'text/event-stream' }, body: JSON.stringify(payload) });
  const reader = res.body.getReader();
  while (true) {
    const {done, value} = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;
    console.log('chunk', new Date().toISOString(), value.length);
  }
})();
Observation: when stall occurs, read() hangs for several seconds even though server logs show write() completed.

Kernel / network probes used: 
- sudo ss -tinp | grep <server-port> to inspect send queue sizes.
- tcpdump -i eth0 -w stall-capture.pcap port 443 and filter later for vsn.
- sudo perf top while the write loop runs (no user CPU spike).

Key log excerpts (server side):
[2026-03-05 14:07:12.117] rpc: gen_token: wrote 128 bytes to socket (non-blocking)
[2026-03-05 14:07:12.121] rpc: gen_token: wrote 136 bytes to socket (non-blocking)
[2026-03-05 14:07:12.122] rpc: gen_token: wrote 140 bytes to socket (non-blocking)
[2026-03-05 14:07:15.423] rpc: gen_token: wrote 120 bytes to socket (non-blocking)
(note the 3s gap in log write timestamps while userland loop still generating tokens)

Client-side capture (node client):
2026-03-05T14:07:12.123Z chunk 128
2026-03-05T14:07:12.125Z chunk 136
2026-03-05T14:07:12.127Z chunk 140
2026-03-05T14:07:15.425Z chunk 120

Hypotheses: 
1) Kernel-level send buffer congestion triggered by small-packet bursts + Nagle interactions; server's non-blocking writes succeed (accepted by kernel) but NIC queue/driver scheduling causes visible drain pauses.
2) Interaction with long-lived TLS sessions + rekeying or TCP timestamps causing transient stall (less likely; no TLS renegotiation seen).
3) Middle-box (load balancer / envoy) applying internal write coalescing or rate-limiting on HTTP/2 or TLS streams — paused flush from proxy side.
4) Unhandled socket quota exhaustion (ephemeral) on egress path causing internal queueing — visible as tcp_send_queue accumulation.
5) A bug in our streaming SDK where writev batching introduces bursts and then sleeps (audit code paths around flush thresholds).

Mitigations tried so far: 
- Forced TCP_NODELAY in runtime for streaming sockets — reduced but did not eliminate stalls.
- Increased SO_SNDBUF on server sockets — small improvement in frequency.
- Swapped to a different envoy config (stream_idle_timeout disabled) in canary; still saw stalls.
- Reproduced on bare VM bypassing envoy (direct to server IP) — stalls still appear (points to host/kernel/NIC).

Next repro steps to run (ordered): 
1) Start server on canary host with extra socket tracing: sudo bpftrace -e 'kprobe:tcp_sendmsg { @[comm] = count(); }'  (capture counts during repro)
2) Run node client with chroma-scale prompt to trigger KV cache hot path (script attached).
3) Simultaneously run: ss -o state established '( sport = :443 )' -i every 1s and log 'sk' send-q.
4) Capture pcap with tcpdump -w and then open in Wireshark to check for persistent ack gaps.
5) If stall reproduces, dump NIC driver ring stats and ethtool -S for interface.

Action items for infra/SRE: 
- Can infra expose per-host NIC queue metrics for the dedicated pool? (asked Luca)
- Add a small agent that exercises many small writes to reproduce on bare-metal hosts (to test driver-level behavior).

Ideas to test (cheap experiments):
- Add a short (1ms) sleep after every N write() calls in server to force kernel scheduling differences and see if stall disappears (if it does, indicates NIC coalescing).
- Try coalesced writes (aggregate several tokens into larger write) vs fine-grained writes to measure difference.
- Experiment with GSO/GRO offload toggles on NIC if we can repro on a lab box.

Random observations / breadcrumbs: 
- Saw similar pattern in a 3rd-party issue where middlware with HTTP/2 flow control caused bursts to queue (link in linked_artifacts).
- On one host, enabling TCP_QUICKACK briefly reduced stall duration (weird).

Notes to self: 
- Keep reproduction scripts minimal and isolate one variable at a time (envoy vs direct, NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED, TCP_NODELAY toggles).
- When filing bug to driver team, include pcap + ss send-q timeline + server write timestamps.

TODO: 
- [ ] Attach node client and a server-side logging build (with write timestamps in microseconds).
- [ ] Run NIC ring stat collection during next canary window.
- [ ] Try reproducing with Python aiohttp client (two different runtimes) to rule out runtime read path.

Scratchpad ends.

-- aria
